stem: A bucket receives thousands of image files a day in mixed formats, and a model team needs each file available as a row carrying its bytes and its path. No parsing of the picture itself is wanted at load time.

option_texts.A: Read them with the binaryFile data source, which turns each file into one record
option_texts.B: Read them as text, which captures the bytes of each picture as a string column
option_texts.C: Read them with a JSON reader, which keeps the metadata and discards the bytes
option_texts.D: Convert each picture to Parquet first, because unstructured bytes cannot be loaded

drill_answer_short: The binaryFile source reads binary files into one record each, holding the raw content and metadata
decision_hinge: The binaryFile data source reads binary files and converts each file into a single record containing the file's raw content and metadata, and it is commonly used to load unstructured data such as images, audio, or PDF files.

plausible_options.B: needs each file available as a row carrying its bytes and its path

eliminated_by.C: No parsing of the picture itself is wanted at load time
eliminated_by.D: thousands of image files a day in mixed formats

distractor_traps.B: T3: confusable sibling - a text reader mangles binary content rather than preserving the raw bytes
distractor_traps.C: T4: breaks a stated requirement - the bytes are exactly what the model team needs
distractor_traps.D: T1: fabricated - unstructured bytes load directly without a conversion step

stem: A query groups enrolments by student and must keep only the students with fewer than three of them. A first attempt also mentioned a column that is neither grouped nor wrapped in an aggregate, and the statement failed.

option_texts.A: HAVING may name any column, grouped or not, so the comparison itself is what failed
option_texts.B: HAVING may name only grouped expressions, aggregates or constants, so the stray column failed
option_texts.C: WHERE should carry the count test, because filtering an aggregate there runs before grouping
option_texts.D: The count test belongs in the select list, because a filter cannot read an aggregate result

drill_answer_short: HAVING expressions may refer only to constants, GROUP BY expressions and aggregate functions
decision_hinge: The expressions specified in the HAVING clause can only refer to constant expressions, expressions that appear in GROUP BY, and aggregate functions; if the expression references columns that are neither in the GROUP BY clause nor wrapped in aggregate functions Databricks raises MISSING_AGGREGATION.

plausible_options.C: must keep only the students with fewer than three of them

eliminated_by.A: a column that is neither grouped nor wrapped in an aggregate
eliminated_by.D: A query groups enrolments by student

distractor_traps.A: T5: common misconception - the clause is restricted precisely so an ungrouped column cannot appear
distractor_traps.C: T3: confusable sibling - WHERE filters rows before grouping and cannot test a group's count
distractor_traps.D: T1: fabricated - a filter clause is exactly where an aggregate result is tested

stem: A single new record has to be added to an existing Delta table while every row already there stays untouched. The team is choosing the statement to run from a SQL editor.

option_texts.A: APPEND VALUES, the statement that adds rows without disturbing the existing ones
option_texts.B: INSERT OVERWRITE with a VALUES clause, which writes the record into the table
option_texts.C: INSERT INTO with a VALUES clause, which adds new rows to the table
option_texts.D: MERGE INTO with a VALUES clause, the only statement that can add a single row

drill_answer_short: INSERT INTO appends rows to a table; INSERT OVERWRITE replaces what is already there
decision_hinge: INSERT INTO appends new rows into a table, whereas INSERT OVERWRITE replaces the existing data in the table with the new rows.

plausible_options.B: A single new record has to be added to an existing Delta table

eliminated_by.A: The team is choosing the statement to run from a SQL editor
eliminated_by.D: every row already there stays untouched

distractor_traps.A: T1: fabricated - there is no APPEND VALUES statement in the SQL dialect
distractor_traps.B: T3: confusable sibling - OVERWRITE does write the record, but it replaces everything else
distractor_traps.D: T5: common misconception - MERGE handles conditional upserts and is not required for a plain add

stem: An owner has to give one group every right that applies to a table rather than naming each one in turn. The group should end up able to do anything the object itself supports.

option_texts.A: GRANT FULL CONTROL on the object, which confers every right the object supports
option_texts.B: GRANT SELECT and MODIFY on the object, since together they cover every right
option_texts.C: GRANT OWNERSHIP of the object, which is how a group receives the full set of rights
option_texts.D: GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES on the object, which grants every privilege applicable to it

drill_answer_short: ALL PRIVILEGES grants all privileges applicable to the securable object
decision_hinge: GRANT grants a privilege on a securable object to a principal, and ALL PRIVILEGES grants all privileges applicable to the securable object.

plausible_options.C: give one group every right that applies to a table

eliminated_by.A: rather than naming each one in turn
eliminated_by.B: able to do anything the object itself supports

distractor_traps.A: T1: fabricated - FULL CONTROL is not a privilege name in this dialect
distractor_traps.B: T2: scope error - two named privileges do not add up to the applicable set
distractor_traps.C: T3: confusable sibling - transferring ownership changes who owns the object rather than granting rights

stem: A production ingest stream must resume exactly where it left off after a restart, without reprocessing files it has already handled. The team is deciding which option carries that progress between runs.

option_texts.A: The checkpoint location, which the stream writes its progress into as it runs
option_texts.B: The schema location, which records both the columns and the files already seen
option_texts.C: The target table history, which the stream reads to recover its progress
option_texts.D: A bookmark column on the source files, which the stream updates after each batch

drill_answer_short: checkpointLocation carries stream progress across restarts; schemaLocation stores the inferred schema
decision_hinge: Auto Loader stores the inferred schema at the cloudFiles.schemaLocation, and the checkpointLocation holds the checkpoint for the streaming query so that it can resume.

plausible_options.B: deciding which option carries that progress between runs

eliminated_by.C: must resume exactly where it left off after a restart
eliminated_by.D: without reprocessing files it has already handled

distractor_traps.B: T3: confusable sibling - the schema location stores the inferred schema, not the ingest progress
distractor_traps.C: T5: common misconception - table history records writes, not which source files were consumed
distractor_traps.D: T1: fabricated - no bookmark is written back onto the source files
